newsitem.title: USA: Cabletron co-founder resigns, new CEO named.
newsitem.headline: Cabletron co-founder resigns, new CEO named.

text.p: Cabletron Systems Inc said Robert Levine, the company's co-founder and current chief executive and president plans to retire December 1 and will be replaced by Don Reed, an executive at NYNEX Corp.
Reed will officially assume his new posts on September 1, the company said.
In 1983, Levine co-founded Cabletron with Craig Benson, the company's chairman and chief operating officer.
The company said Benson will continue in his role as chairman, focusing on strategic company issues, while migrating day-to-day operating responsibilities to Reed.
Levine will support Reed in the transition of leadership through November, it said.
The news sent Cabletron shares higher at the opening of trading Wednesday morning. The stock traded at 37-7/16, up 5/8 of a a point from Tuesday's close.

Cabletron was a pioneer in the development of local area network equipment industry and remains a leading supplier of network hub equipment used to interconnect local computer networks, typically in large offices or department workgroups.
The company has moved in recent years to expand its focus to include wide area networking products used by telephone carriers and large corporations to create far-flung networks.

But Cabletron must first staunch the declining market share in its core hub business, which has lost ground to competing network switching technology that offers similar functions, often at lower cost.
In a statement, Benson praised Reed's experience in key markets in which Cabletron now operates and in operating several divisions at NYNEX, a multi-billion phone company.

"With the rapid convergence of voice, video and data, Don Reed's extensive telecommunications experience as a 30-year veteran of NYNEX, including service as President and CEO of one of its major operating units, provides Cabletron with expert knowledge in key markets," Benson said.

At NYNEX, Reed was named president and group executive of NYNEX in January 1995. Prior to this, he was president and chief executive officer for NYNEX in New England since 1993 and executive vice president and chief operating officer of New England Telephone since April 1991.
He was also president of NYNEX Information Resources Company, the corporation's telephone directory publishing subsidiary, in the late 80's. Reed joined New England Telephone in 1966.
